column1: # Call-count fingerprint groups: NAME <TAB> REGEX
# One regex per logical component, matched against the symbol names in BOTH
# engines' callgrind profiles, and the matches summed. Each row is the claim
# "mcfish calls this as many times as Stockfish does" -- which is a claim about the
# ALGORITHM, not about cost, and is immune to inlining as long as the symbol
# survives on both sides.
# CHOOSE SYMBOLS THAT SURVIVE INLINING ON BOTH SIDES. A group whose regex matches
# nothing on one side is reported as a MISS and fails, because a silent zero on one
# side would read as a divergence forever. If a symbol gets inlined away by a
# compiler change, fix the row rather than deleting the check -- and prefer a
# callee that is too big to inline over its caller.
# What this is FOR: a call-count divergence is an algorithm bug and outranks every
# cost finding. Two real defects were found this way and by nothing else -- a
# `ucinewgame` that discarded the position, and a terminal root that skipped the
# per-worker reset -- both of which every value gate passed over, because neither
# changed a node count on any position anyone had thought to test.
